Loopback to builder: test_s1_malformed_entry_fails_validation (line 58): Test is skipped due to incorrect import. Tries to import 'load_knowledge' which doesn't exist - should import 'load_builtin_knowledge' instead. The implementation exists (anvil/knowledge.py:52), so this test should run and validate that malformed entries fail with file and entry named.; test_s10_guide_designation_names_design_model (line 548): Test is skipped due to incorrect import. Tries to import 'load_routing_policy()' which doesn't exist - should either import and call 'get_design_model_from_routing()' or access MODEL_POLICY directly from anvil.routing. The routing policy exists (anvil/routing.py:18-25), so this test should run and validate that stations reference the design model.; test_s1_builtin_dataset_exists_and_validates (line 33): Test checks that data files exist and contain valid JSON, but never calls load_builtin_knowledge() to validate that the loader actually works. Per the standing note 'Tests must be real: every test calls the implementation it names and asserts behavior', this test should call load_builtin_knowledge() and assert it succeeds without validation errors.; S10 guide designation not wired into runtime: The station.json files declare 'guided': true and 'designation': 'guided design station' for builder, reviewer-design, and writer, but the Station dataclass in anvil/stations.py (line 9-21) does not include a 'guided' field. When load_registry loads station.json files, this field is dropped. The runner (anvil/runner.py lines 483-486) has no way to detect guided stations and apply the design model from routing policy. The function get_design_model_from_routing exists in knowledge.py (lines 499-506) but is never called. Fix: add 'guided' field to Station dataclass, preserve it in load_registry, and in runner.py apply the design model from routing policy when station.guided is True.; S10 test references non-existent function: tests/test_design_knowledge.py test_s10_guide_designation_names_design_model (line 548) tries to import load_routing_policy from anvil.routing, but this function does not exist in routing.py. The test will skip rather than validating the requirement. The routing.py module has MODEL_POLICY dict and load_routing_config function, but no load_routing_policy. Either the test should use the correct function name or a load_routing_policy wrapper should be added.; S10 hardcoded models contradict requirement: The loopback finding states 'the station catalogs must stop hardcoding a design model string' and 'no model name is duplicated across station.json files', yet builder/station.json has 'model': 'fast-builder', reviewer-design/station.json has 'model': 'review-balanced', and writer/station.json has 'model': 'writing-strong'. These are not duplicates but they are hardcoded values. The requirement says the guide designation should read the model 'at the point of use' from routing policy. The current architecture applies station.model from the catalog (runner.py line 483) with no check for guided stations. The routing policy defines 'designer': 'openai/gpt-6-astra' (routing.py line 24) as the design model, but guided stations never use it.
